hypothesis: Windows in-place updater leaves bootstrap/app-base.zip stale, causing next startup to restore old files
action: traced updater_main.py in-place branch and runtime_manager.copy_payload_for_in_place() marker logic
result: updater wrote installed files from downloaded payload but .payload-ready was computed from old bootstrap/app-base.zip; startup extraction source remained old zip

hypothesis: Copy downloaded payload into bootstrap/app-base.zip before writing .payload-ready prevents rollback
action: added regression test for Windows in-place update with old bootstrap zip and new downloaded payload
result: test asserts installed VERSION/main.py, bootstrap/app-base.zip VERSION, and .payload-ready all advance to the new payload

hypothesis: If bootstrap payload refresh fails, startup can still prevent rollback by comparing bootstrap VERSION with installed VERSION
action: added guard in copy_payload_for_in_place() and tests for stale bootstrap skip
result: launcher skips extraction when bootstrap app-base.zip VERSION is lower than install VERSION; same-version bootstrap can still repair stale files

hypothesis: Bootstrap payload refresh failure should not fail the already-applied in-place update
action: wrapped updater bootstrap copy in non-blocking warning path and added regression test
result: updater returns 0, installed VERSION/main.py advance, stale bootstrap remains old, warning is emitted to stderr
